transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’ve been very self-conscious about a scar on my wrist. I know it probably doesn’t look as bad to other people as it does to me, but at church or when I’m playing bridge, I feel like everyone notices it right away.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking, hiding, or covering the scar?

Yes. Before I go out, I’ll look at my wrist in the hall mirror a few times. I try different sleeves or wear a bracelet over it, and sometimes I ask my husband whether it looks obvious. He always tells me it’s barely noticeable, but I still worry about it.
When people might notice your wrist, are you mainly afraid they’ll judge you negatively because of it?
Yes, I do. I know it may not look that bad to other people, but at church or bridge I feel like people’s eyes go straight to my wrist—like it’s the first thing they notice about me.
If your wrist looked completely normal, would you still feel very anxious about being judged by people at church or while playing bridge?

No, I don’t think so. It’s really the scar that makes me feel that way. I keep thinking people’s eyes go right to my wrist, even though I know it probably stands out more to me than it does to anyone else.
